newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Canada investment in Indonesia to continue-envoy.
newsitem.headline: Canada investment in Indonesia to continue-envoy.

text.p: The controversy over the huge Busang gold deposit involving two Canadian mining companies will have no impact on the country's investment in Indonesia, Canada's ambassador said Tuesday.

"I think Canadian companies are bullish on investing in Indonesia. There will be some hiccups, but I am hoping we are going to be able to overcome whatever differences there are," Ambassador Gary Smith told a news conference.

Last week, Indonesia urged Canada's Barrick Gold Corp. and Bre-X Minerals Ltd. to agree to a proposal to jointly develop the 57-million-ounce Busang deposit in Indonesia's east Kalimantan province, which is worth about $21 billion.

In November, the government asked Bre-X, which controls the deposit, to form a joint venture with Barrick. The proposal would leave Bre-X with 22.5 percent and give Barrick 67.5 percent and the government 10 percent.
Smith said differences over the issue had been dealt with and that more Canadian companies were poised to invest in Indonesia's mining industry.
"Indonesia certainly has come up on the horizon and we're ready to move forward here in a major way," he said.
He said more than 60 Canadian mining exploration companies were waiting for their contracts of work from the Indonesian mining and energy ministry. He gave no other details.

Barrick and Bre-X said in December they had reached basic agreement on Jakarta's proposal but said they wanted Indonesia's guidance on a few issues and the government's stamp of approval before announcing the deal to shareholders.
Analysts said in Toronto Monday a decision could be reached this week.

Smith said Canadian investment in Indonesia totalled C$6.4 billion ($4.7 billion) and was expected to grow to C$8 billion ($5.9 billion) in the next two years. The main sectors of investment included oil and gas, mining, pulp and paper and footwear, he said.
Smith also said Canada hoped to start an air link with Indonesia this year and carriers, which have an air agreement in place, from both countries are in talks on possible routes.

He said Garuda Indonesia and Air Canada had not yet decided where aircraft flying from Jakarta, Indonesia, to Vancouver, British Columbia, and vice versa should refuel and added that the Canadian carrier expected to have three flights a week.
Smith was speaking at the announcement of a series of events to be held in Indonesia in connection with Canada's "Year of Asia Pacific" aimed at promoting relations with Asian countries.
